h1: BP Grand Tower Hotel — A 3-Star Downtown Hotel That Sells Location and Price Near Lee Gardens Hat Yai
intro: If you're on a budget but want to stay in the heart of Hat Yai, within walking distance of the markets and malls, BP Grand Tower Hotel is a name that comes up often on lists of cheaper stays. It's a long-established high-rise on Sanehanusorn Road, opened back in 1991 and given a major renovation in 2015. With about 251 rooms, it has an outdoor pool, a fitness centre and free parking. Lee Gardens Plaza is about 5 minutes' walk, with Central Department Store and Kim Yong Market close by. Rates start from approx. THB 900/night, and it scores 7.7 from around 210 reviews — its draw is location and price; newness is something you accept.

body.html: The main reason people choose BP Grand Tower is its downtown location at an easy-to-reach price · the hotel sits on Sanehanusorn Road, about 5 minutes' walk to Lee Gardens Plaza, close to Central Department Store and Kim Yong Market, the hub of Hat Yai's food scene · the surrounding streets are packed with restaurants, massage shops and convenience stores, so you find food the moment you step out · for visitors here mainly to browse markets and shop, this location does the job at a lower budget than the big-brand hotels in the same district.

It's a high-rise with around 251 rooms, from Superior and Deluxe up to Executive and suites · many rooms are larger than you'd expect at this price, with air conditioning, a fridge, a TV and free Wi-Fi · higher floors give a broad view over Hat Yai, and several reviews praise the space and cleanliness relative to the rate · just understand this is an older building, with classic older-hotel furnishings and decor rather than a sleek new design.
"Great location — easy walk to Lee Gardens and Central, plenty of food around. The room was bigger and cleaner than I expected for the price, and the staff were friendly."

The shared facilities are enough for this class of hotel · an outdoor pool, a fitness centre, a restaurant and a 24-hour front desk · free parking is a real plus for self-drivers, since parking in downtown Hat Yai is scarce and pricey · free Wi-Fi is in every room and laundry service is available · the pool is small, more for a cooling dip than resort-style lounging, but many guests say it's nice to have one at all at this price point.

The trade-off to accept is that the building is ageing and shows clear wear · some reviews note damp walls or a musty smell in certain rooms, especially after rain, dusty or dated furniture in places, and weak hot water in some bathrooms · breakfast is another point several reviews call average rather than a highlight · if you expect a room that feels brand new, this isn't it — but treat it as a budget stay with a great location and your expectations will line up far better with what you get.

Rates start around THB 900/night for a standard room in regular periods, rising to roughly THB 1,200–1,600 for larger rooms or suites, and over long weekends — when Malaysian and Singaporean visitors flood Hat Yai — prices climb quickly and rooms sell out fast · a score of 7.7 from around 210 Trip.com reviews captures it well: location and value score high, while room condition and breakfast pull the score down · on Tripadvisor it sits near the bottom of the Hat Yai list, consistent with an older budget hotel rather than a premium pick.

In short, BP Grand Tower Hotel suits budget travellers, market-and-shopping visitors, and self-drivers who want free parking in the centre · if what you need is a clean place to sleep in a great location at a low price, leaving more budget for food and sightseeing, it does the job well · but if you prioritise sleek new rooms, good breakfast or a resort feel, add to your budget and look at a 4-star in the same district instead.

A tip from the reviews: ask for a higher floor and a recently renovated room to avoid the musty-smell and damp issues · mention in advance if you want strong hot water, and ask whether a renovated room is available · always book a Free Cancellation rate, and check for extra charges such as an additional-bed fee before you confirm · reserve several weeks ahead over long weekends, when rooms fill fast.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — BP Grand Tower Hotel Hat Yai

faq.q: Where is BP Grand Tower Hotel and how do I get there?
faq.a: It's at 74 Sanehanusorn Road in downtown Hat Yai, Songkhla · about 5 minutes' walk to Lee Gardens Plaza and Central Department Store, and 7–8 minutes to Kim Yong Market · roughly 5 minutes by car from Hat Yai Railway Station and about 25 minutes from Hat Yai Airport (HDY).

faq.q: What are the room rates and room types at BP Grand Tower Hotel?
faq.a: Rates start around THB 900/night for a Superior in regular periods · Deluxe at about THB 1,100, Executive at about THB 1,400 and a Suite at about THB 1,800 · prices depend on season and rise quickly on long weekends, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Who is BP Grand Tower Hotel best for?
faq.a: It suits budget travellers, market-and-shopping visitors, and self-drivers who want free downtown parking · it stands out for location and price · it's less ideal for those after sleek new rooms or a resort feel.

faq.q: Is the hotel old · what should I know before booking?
faq.a: It's an older building, opened in 1991 and renovated in 2015 · some reviews note damp or musty rooms after rain, dated furniture in places, and an average breakfast · ask for a higher floor or renovated room and pick a Free Cancellation package · location and value still score well.

faq.q: Does BP Grand Tower Hotel have a pool and parking?
faq.a: Yes to both · there's an outdoor pool (small, for a cooling dip), a fitness centre and free parking · free parking is a real plus in downtown Hat Yai where parking is scarce · every room has free Wi-Fi and there's a 24-hour front desk.

faq.q: Can I walk to Lee Gardens and Kim Yong Market from BP Grand Tower Hotel?
faq.a: Yes · Lee Gardens Plaza and Central are about 5 minutes' walk, and Kim Yong Market about 7–8 minutes · the streets around the hotel are full of restaurants, massage shops and convenience stores, making it easy to explore downtown on foot without a car.
